connections.why: Scarcity forces the choices that rational economic agents are assumed to make
Markets are one way societies answer the basic questions of scarcity
Demand is one of the two forces that together determine market price
Supply is the other force that interacts with demand to set price
Markets work through the interaction of demand and supply
The degree of competition shapes the prices firms can charge
Productivity and costs of production determine how much firms supply
The division of labour links production to the demand for workers
Labour is a derived demand stemming from demand for goods
A lack of competition is one source of market failure
Monetary policy operates through money, interest rates and financial markets
Growth in output tends to reduce unemployment
Rapid growth can generate inflationary pressure on prices
Fiscal policy is a key tool for meeting government objectives
Monetary policy is used to pursue stability and growth objectives
Supply-side measures aim to raise the economy's productive potential
Market failure provides the rationale for government intervention
Supply-side policies work by raising productivity and capacity
Trade flows are recorded in the balance of payments
Exchange rates affect the competitiveness of exports and imports
Globalisation has greatly expanded the volume of world trade
Controlling inflation is the primary aim of monetary policy
